conflicts.point: Whether pre-market certification and safety verification gates serve as necessary protections against severe biological or recursive risks or function primarily as anticompetitive regulatory capture mechanisms.

positions.stance: Mandatory pre-market certification and safety verification gates are necessary to prevent catastrophic biological and autonomous system risks.
Pre-market certification requirements act as bureaucratic tollbooths that protect incumbents and delay vital medical and scientific discoveries.

conflicts.point: Whether post-market inspection statutes and supply-chain provenance tracking are sufficient to manage dual-use biological risks without requiring ex-ante model licensing.

positions.stance: Post-market facility audits and open API provenance tracking can govern dual-use risks without erecting pre-market licensing monopolies.
Post-market measures are insufficient to catch fast-moving biological threats generated by unmonitored chemical synthesis models.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-market certification and safety verification gates serve as necessary protections against severe biological risks or function primarily as anticompetitive regulatory capture mechanisms.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position relies on well-documented historical precedents in telecommunications where infrastructure bottlenecks allowed incumbent firms to dictate market terms to smaller innovators. By contrast, the safetyist argument treats hardware concentration as a natural safety boundary without providing empirical proof that rigid compute ceilings successfully intercept specific biological threats better than algorithmic audits.

verdicts.conflict: Whether post-market inspection statutes and supply-chain provenance tracking are sufficient to manage dual-use biological risks without requiring ex-ante model licensing.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position successfully references concrete existing legal frameworks like 21 U.S.C. Section 360 to demonstrate how physical facility audits and API provenance tracking can govern dual-use risks. The accelerationist and safetyist positions rely on more abstract claims about bureaucratic tollbooths or catastrophic risks without detailing workable ex-ante administrative mechanisms.
